newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia shares ease on profit-taking, trend unclear.
newsitem.headline: Russia shares ease on profit-taking, trend unclear.

text.p: Russian shares slipped in early trade on Friday on domestic profit-taking, traders said, and Western investors fixed an anxious eye on a sliding Dow Jones. Opinions differed on the market trend for next week.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index slipped to 421.08 after Thursday's closing 421.68, while on Wall Street the Dow Jones index fell 36 points to close on Thursday at 7654.
"For some time we've not seen a correlation with the Dow Jones -- now we're feeling a correlation," said Prospekt chief trader Andrei Ippolitov.

National power company UES EESR.RTS dipped to $0.3630 at 0840 GMT from Thursday's close of $0.3650 and oil company LUKoil LKOH.RTS, which has seen spectacular gains in the past week and a half, eased to $19.70 from $19.80.
Dealers saw the market dropping one to two percent by the end of the trading session as Russian brokers took profits.
"Some illiquid shares are still very much in demand...but there is selling pressure (from Russian brokers) in liquid stock," said CentreInvest director of equity sales Dan Rapoport.
"There are no large (Western) sell orders at this point but I have seen big blocks of liquid shares walking the market."
Prospekt's Ippolitov said the downward trend could be reversed as soon as next week, but opinions varied.
"It's difficult to say whether this is a major decline or just a small hiccup -- it's all going to depend on what happens today," said Rapoport.
"When investors see a correction coming they tend to sit on the sidelines...on the other hand it could be a hiccup along the way and investors will see this as the time to buy," he added.
